title: TAROM's first Boeing 737 MAX signals the start of a long-awaited fleet renewal programme
description:
First Boeing 737 MAX 8 delivered to TAROM The first aircraft arrived in Bucharest after being ferried from Seattle via Keflavík in Iceland.
TAROM will fly its 737 MAX fleet on routes connecting Bucharest with major European capitals, “providing an enhanced passenger experience,” according to the carrier.
TAROM originally announced an order for five Boeing 737 MAX 8s on July 16, 2018, in a deal valued by Boeing at $586 million at list prices.
Under the restructuring programme, TAROM ultimately planned to introduce four 737 MAX 8s through a mixture of operating and financial leases.
Marking the start of a fleet revitalisation For TAROM, the significance of the 737 MAX goes beyond the arrival of a single new aircraft.
text:
Romania’s national airline, TAROM, has entered a new chapter with the arrival of its first Boeing 737 MAX 8, marking the beginning of a major fleet refresh intended to make the carrier smaller, more efficient and more competitive.

The new aircraft, registered YR-BGO and named Mircea Lucescu, was formally delivered to TAROM on 12 September 2026 and is the first 737 MAX to enter service with a Romanian airline.

First Boeing 737 MAX 8 delivered to TAROM

The first aircraft arrived in Bucharest after being ferried from Seattle via Keflavík in Iceland. A second MAX is expected to follow shortly, with the four-aircraft programme scheduled to be completed by 2027. TAROM has also indicated that it is looking beyond those four aircraft, with discussions around potentially adding another MAX later in the decade.

The new aircraft is particularly significant because TAROM has been operating a relatively small and ageing fleet while undergoing a substantial restructuring. TAROM will fly its 737 MAX fleet on routes connecting Bucharest with major European capitals, “providing an enhanced passenger experience,” according to the carrier.

The arrival of the airline’s new 737 MAX 8 is not simply an additional aircraft but represents the replacement of older-generation Boeing narrowbodies and is central to a plan to simplify the fleet, reduce operating costs, and better compete with the likes of Wizz Air, HiSky, AnimaWings and Ryanair in the Romanian market.

TAROM’s current fleet illustrates why renewal is necessary. Before the MAX’s arrival, the carrier’s mainline fleet consisted of Boeing 737-700s and 737-800s alongside ATR 72 turboprops.

Current fleet data shows three 737-700s, four 737-800s, two ATR 72-500s, and four ATR 72-600s. The 737-700s, in particular, are among the aircraft targeted for replacement by the new-generation MAX.

The fleet is vastly different from TAROM’s larger operation of previous decades. Indeed, the European Commission’s restructuring documentation describes how the airline had a fleet of 29 aircraft before the rationalisation programme, including Boeing 737-300s and 737-700s, Airbus A318s, and a sizeable ATR fleet.

The restructuring plan envisaged reducing that fleet substantially while concentrating operations around a smaller number of aircraft types.

This first arrival has been much anticipated

The MAX order itself has had a long history, with the delivery of the first aircraft much anticipated. TAROM originally announced an order for five Boeing 737 MAX 8s on July 16, 2018, in a deal valued by Boeing at $586 million at list prices. At the time, the aircraft were expected to be delivered over the following years.

The programme subsequently became entangled with TAROM’s financial difficulties, restructuring and the wider disruption to the aviation industry. Rather than simply receiving the five aircraft originally announced, the current fleet-renewal plan has evolved around leased aircraft.

In 2024, TAROM and CDB Aviation announced agreements covering two new 737 MAX 8s from CDB Aviation’s Boeing orderbook. Those aircraft were originally scheduled for delivery between December 2025 and January 2026 and were to be configured with 189 seats.

Under the restructuring programme, TAROM ultimately planned to introduce four 737 MAX 8s through a mixture of operating and financial leases. The European Commission described the MAX as replacing the airline’s outgoing 737-700s and helping create a more streamlined and uniform fleet.

The objective was not just to acquire newer aircraft, but to achieve lower operating costs, greater efficiency and a more consistent passenger product.

That makes the first MAX especially important. Boeing says the 737-8 offers roughly 20% lower fuel consumption and carbon emissions than the aircraft it replaces, while giving TAROM a modern narrowbody capable of operating both domestic and European routes efficiently.

Marking the start of a fleet revitalisation

For TAROM, the significance of the 737 MAX goes beyond the arrival of a single new aircraft. It is the visible beginning of a fleet transformation that has been years in the making.

The carrier is moving away from a heterogeneous fleet assembled over several generations towards a smaller, more standardised operation built around modern Boeing 737s and ATR turboprops.

The challenge will be turning that new equipment into sustainable growth. TAROM remains in the middle of a restructuring programme, and its relatively small fleet leaves little room for operational disruption.

But the arrival of the MAX gives the Romanian flag carrier an important tool for the next phase – a modern, fuel-efficient aircraft capable of replacing some of its oldest narrowbodies while improving efficiency across its European network. After years of waiting, TAROM’s fleet renewal is finally becoming tangible.

BANYUMAS – Padatnya aktivitas pada hari kerja kerap membuat masyarakat kesulitan meluangkan waktu untuk menyelesaikan urusan administrasi pemerintahan, termasuk urusan pertanahan. Salah satunya dirasakan Vivi Lestari, warga Kabupaten Banyumas, yang mengaku terbantu karena dapat menyelesaikan proses alih media sertipikat di hari libur.

“Karena kesibukan di Senin-Jumat itu kadang susah sekali ya kita bisa keluar untuk menyelesaikan permasalahan-permasalahan pertanahan. Saya berterima kasih sekali kepada ATR/BPN Banyumas yang sudah sangat membantu untuk layanan PELATARAN ini,” ujar Vivi Lestari, saat ditemui di Kantah Kabupaten Banyumas.

Vivi Lestari yang merupakan pegawai di Universitas Jenderal Soedirman (Unsoed) mengatakan, layanan pertanahan pada akhir pekan ini akan bermanfaat bagi masyarakat, utamanya pekerja kantoran. Layanan ini membantunya mengurus keperluan pertanahan di tengah aktivitas yang harus dijalani pada hari kerja.

“Dan kali ini saya mendapatkan layanan alih media di hari Sabtu, sangat membantu sekali. Semoga ATR/BPN Banyumas layanannya semakin mantap. Terima kasih,” kata Vivi Lestari.

PELATARAN menyediakan beberapa layanan pertanahan yang bisa dimanfaatkan masyarakat. Selain pengambilan produk, di akhir pekan masyarakat juga bisa berkonsultasi terkait urusan pertanahan.

Layanan akhir pekan ini juga jadi pilihan bagi Andi, warga Kabupaten Ngawi, untuk mencari-cari informasi mengenai proses balik nama sertipikat tanah waris.

“Dengan adanya pelayanan akhir pekan ini, saya merasa terbantu dan informasi yang diberikan petugas sangat informatif dan jelas. Terima kasih, semoga BPN Ngawi semakin maju,” tutur Andi.

PELATARAN bisa menjadi pilihan bagi masyarakat yang memiliki keperluan pertanahan, namun kesulitan meluangkan waktu pada hari kerja. Melalui layanan ini, Kementerian Agraria dan Tata Ruang/Badan Pertanahan Nasional (ATR/BPN) berupaya menghadirkan layanan yang lebih mudah diakses masyarakat dan bisa memenuhi kebutuhan masyarakat. (LS/JR)

text:
Dubai: Etihad Airways CEO Antonoaldo Neves has one major concern as the airline heads into the final months of 2026: jet fuel prices. Demand is not keeping him awake. Fuel is.

“I think jet fuel keeps me awake,” Neves told Gulf News on the sidelines of the opening day of the Arabian Travel Market in Dubai, as the Abu Dhabi airline continues to expand its fleet, network and workforce.

For Neves, the biggest risk facing Etihad is not demand but the cost of jet fuel — and what sustained high prices could mean for airfares next year.

He said the key question for Etihad is now what happens to the average fare next year if jet fuel prices remain elevated, particularly as airlines across the Gulf, Europe and the US compete heavily for passengers.

“So we compete a lot, right? And every time you compete a lot, the competition level is high. You cannot pass on prices as easy as you are in other markets.”

“If you ask me, what is my thinking right now in terms of risk challenge? It’s what’s going to happen with the average fare next year because of jet fuel price,” he said.

Jet fuel was around $170 a barrel, according to the International Air Transport Association's (IATA) jet fuel monitor, according to Neves, who said the crack spread — the difference between the price of crude oil and refined products such as jet fuel — was also high.

However, he said the forward curve was indicating a less severe picture than current prices and argued that the present spike was unlikely to be sustainable.

“I hope jet fuel price goes back to normal levels,” he said. “The forward curve is saying that the jet fuel forward curve is not great, but it’s not as bad as the jet fuel right now.”

Neves pointed to the sharp move in fuel prices during the recent regional disruption as evidence of how quickly the market can change.

“We had the situation about six months ago, right? And jet fuel went back to 110 in July, so it’s going to come back. It’s not sustainable, right? So it’s just volatility because of the situation, the global situation.”

Fuel concern

Etihad is partly protected by fuel hedging, but it remains exposed to movements in the market. Neves said the current fuel environment is being driven by a wider global situation, rather than the Middle East alone, pointing to developments in Russia and Ukraine as factors that are also affecting oil prices.

“I hope jet fuel price goes back to normal levels,” he said, adding that the current situation was not sustainable. He said the forward curve suggested prices could eventually ease, although the airline still has to manage the impact of current prices.

For passengers, the key question is whether higher fuel costs will eventually appear in ticket prices.

Neves said that will depend partly on how much pricing power individual airlines have. Stronger airlines could benefit if fares rise, while weaker carriers that cannot generate enough demand could come under greater pressure.

“Elasticity plays,” he said. However, he cautioned against trying to predict exactly how the market will respond, saying conditions can change quickly, as airlines experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Flights full

For now, Etihad is seeing strong demand, with Neves repeatedly describing the airline’s flights as “full, full, full”.

The carrier’s load factor reached 92 per cent last month, he said, despite several international travel advisories remaining in place.

Etihad’s flights from Europe to the UAE are full, while its services from the US are also performing strongly, said the CEO. The airline is preparing to launch Calgary as it continues rebuilding and expanding its network.

“I understand countries take time to remove travel advisories,” Neves said. But he believes travellers are increasingly making their own decisions based on the experiences of friends and other passengers who have already travelled to the UAE.

“People understand that governments take longer to remove these travel advisories,” he said. “If you want to travel, their friends travel and they say, ‘OK, travel. It was great.’”

He also pointed to Etihad’s operational performance during the disruption, saying the airline did not cancel flights at the last minute or move customers away from services.

“Word of mouth, and I think the great track record that we have in these situations also help,” he said.

More flights

Etihad is now operating 320 flights a day, which Neves said is 20 per cent more than last year. The airline spent the first three months of the year gradually bringing capacity back, moving through 30 per cent, 40 per cent and 70 per cent levels before reaching 100 per cent capacity by July.

The past three months have been particularly strong.

In July, Etihad had 17 per cent more capacity than in July 2025, while the airline also made more money that month than it did in July last year.

August was slightly weaker because of fuel prices, but Neves said the performance across July and August gave Etihad “strength and certainty that the strategy is in the right place”.

September has also started strongly, with the CEO saying the airline's flights are continuing to fill up.

Fleet doubles

The airline is continuing to expand rapidly, with Etihad expecting to finish this year with around 140 aircraft, compared with 70 in 2022.

“In four years we doubled the number of aircraft,” Neves said. “We’re really proud of that. I don’t know any other airline in the world our size that has doubled in four years.”

Around 15 aircraft are due to arrive in the second half of this year. The majority are narrow-body aircraft, while the airline is also expecting A350s and other wide-body aircraft.

Several of the incoming narrow-bodies will be A321LRs, which have become an important part of Etihad’s network strategy. And for Etihad investing in newer-generation aircraft that consume less fuel is a more immediate and practical route to improving efficiency.

“The most important thing I can do is to invest in new aircraft type to burn less fuel per flight per hour,” he said, adding that new-generation aircraft can use about 20 per cent less fuel per passenger.

“There is no sustainable aviation fuel in the world that can solve for that.”

Etihad spends about $2 billion a year on new aircraft, while its annual fuel bill is also around $2 billion, Neves said. "Whenever SAF is available, and whenever SAF is is at the right market price, we we can buy it," said the aviation veteran.

China, Africa

The aircraft arriving now are also helping Etihad prepare for another phase of growth, with China and Africa set to be major areas of focus next year. “Everywhere is important, but we stagger the growth so that we can focus,” Neves said. “So next year is China and Africa.”

The airline is using the A321LR to help increase frequencies as well as serve longer routes. Neves said Etihad now has double-daily services to almost all destinations in Europe, while Bangkok has reached five flights a day.

He said the narrow-body aircraft makes those frequencies possible and allows the airline to offer more choice to passengers without relying exclusively on larger wide-body aircraft.

“Schedule and frequency is a very important part of a product,” he said.

Break-even target

Despite the rapid expansion, Etihad is targeting a break-even result this year. Neves said the airline could make a small profit or lose a small amount depending on fuel-price volatility, but stressed that profitability is not the main priority for 2026.

“The most important thing this year is cash flow generation,” he said.

The airline needs to generate cash to fund its capital spending, including new aircraft, while Neves said Etihad is in a comfortable financial position with a strong balance sheet and “almost zero” bank debt.

“We’re going to get stronger out of the situation,” he said.

Hiring drive

The expansion is also creating jobs. Etihad hired more than 600 people during March, April and May, including pilots and cabin crew, and Neves said the airline expects to add another 600 employees during the second half of the year.

The longer-term hiring plan is considerably bigger.

Etihad expects to hire around 1,500 people every year for the next five years, as it continues adding aircraft to its fleet.

“We’re adding 20 planes per year every year,” Neves said, explaining that each aircraft requires around 60 to 70 additional employees.

Around 200 of those annual hires would be pilots, he said.

Premium push

A major takeaway? It is evident that Etihad is propping up its premium segment in a big way. Neves’ comments came as Etihad unveiled its new-look seats and wider Beyond Borders customer experience at ATM on Monday.

Neves said the airline is putting a major emphasis on premium travel as it looks to move the customer experience into its next generation.

The new look will eventually extend across the journey, from online interactions and airport check-in to lounges, boarding and the onboard experience. Etihad also introduced its Wellbeing offering last week.

title: Beyond the Visible: How Pall Aerospace Powers the Future of Flight | Aviation Week
description:
Small Components, Critical Responsibility Aerospace progress is often measured by faster aircraft, longer range, and new propulsion systems.
During the 1960s, the company developed disposable glass fiber depth media, which became an aviation filtration standard.
Pall also advanced engine air protection through its Centrisep Engine Air Protection Systems that later become known as Pall PUREair systems.
Pall filtration systems today support a broad range of helicopter fleets, reflecting decades of application experience across demanding environments.
Pall has participated in testing involving 100 percent sustainable aviation fuel on systems associated with Rolls-Royce Trent 700 and Trent XWB engines.
text:
Small Components, Critical Responsibility

Aerospace progress is often measured by faster aircraft, longer range, and new propulsion systems. Yet many advances depend on technologies that rarely attract attention. Filtration is one of them. By controlling contamination in fluids, air, and fuel, filtration helps protect critical systems, support reliability, and enable aircraft to operate in demanding environments. For nearly eight decades, Pall Corporation has contributed to this essential engineering discipline across commercial aviation, defense, rotorcraft, and space exploration.

The story began with Dr. David B. Pall, a chemist who developed a stainless-steel mesh filter to address the limitations of paper media used in early aircraft hydraulic systems. Responding to the need for more dependable protection on Boeing 707 aircraft, he created the sintered wire cloth Rigimesh filter. The technology offered a more effective way to safeguard hydraulic systems from contamination and established a foundation for continued aerospace innovation.

Pall soon challenged its own approach. During the 1960s, the company developed disposable glass fiber depth media, which became an aviation filtration standard. The work also reached beyond atmospheric flight. NASA engineers selected Pall technology for the Apollo program, including a porous metal heat exchanger used in Neil Armstrong’s spacesuit during the Apollo 11 mission. Pall also supplied Air filters that helped protect the lunar module atmosphere during cabin pressure equalization.

These applications demonstrate a recurring principle in aerospace engineering: components that may appear small can carry major responsibility. Effective contamination control protects more than equipment. It can support mission continuity, system performance, and the people who depend on both.

Protecting Rotorcraft in the Harshest Conditions

That principle became especially important in rotorcraft. In the early 1970s, Pall introduced a three micron, absolute rated filter for helicopter transmission systems. The technology enhanced lubricant system reliability and became a selected solution for the Chinook helicopter fleet. Pall also advanced engine air protection through its Centrisep Engine Air Protection Systems that later become known as Pall PUREair systems. These systems were developed to reduce the threat posed by particulate, sand and debris entering helicopter engines in some of the harshest operating conditions.

The challenge remains highly relevant. Rotorcraft often operate close to the ground, where dust and particulate concentrations can be severe. Missions may involve military operations, humanitarian support, rescue, or transport in remote locations. In each case, protecting the engine and transmission from contamination can help operators pursue availability, durability, and maintainability objectives. Pall filtration systems today support a broad range of helicopter fleets, reflecting decades of application experience across demanding environments.

Raising the Standard for Cabin Air

Commercial aviation introduced another challenge: cabin air quality. As air travel became more accessible during the 1980s, Pall engineers developed filtration technology for aircraft cabins. Within two years, the company’s filters became the first to qualify as HEPA rated cabin air filters, according to Pall’s historical materials. Continued microbial testing contributed to True HEPA filters by 1998, followed by Advanced Cabin Air Filters that combined HEPA and odor removal capabilities.

Pall also contributed to the development of industry practices, including the first European pre-standard on aircraft cabin air quality in 2004. The company later achieved certification for cockpit air filters designed to remove particulates and volatile organic compounds. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Pall’s PUREair cabin solutions and HEPA filtration capabilities underscored the importance of high efficiency particle removal in shared aircraft environments.

Preparing Filtration for New Energy Pathways

The next era of aviation will require filtration to address different fluids, contaminants, materials, and operating conditions. Sustainable aviation fuel is one example. Pall has participated in testing involving 100 percent sustainable aviation fuel on systems associated with Rolls-Royce Trent 700 and Trent XWB engines. This work reflects the need to evaluate established aircraft technologies as the industry considers lower carbon energy pathways.

Hydrogen powered flight creates another frontier. Pall Aerospace has been named as a key filtration provider in European Commission research projects linked to future Hydrogen powered flight and continue to push the envelope of what is possible for particulate and chemical filtration in the next generation of fuel cell propulsion systems.

The significance extends beyond a single project. Fuel cell propulsion introduces contamination control requirements that differ from conventional aircraft architectures. Particulates and chemical contaminants can threaten sensitive systems, making filtration an enabling consideration rather than a secondary component. By developing and validating solutions for this environment, Pall is applying nearly 80 years of aerospace experience to a new propulsion challenge.

Collaboration Turns Ambition into Flight-Ready Systems

This progression also shows why collaboration matters. Aerospace innovation rarely happens through one technology or organization. Aircraft manufacturers, propulsion specialists, research institutions, suppliers, and regulators must translate ambitious concepts into systems that can be tested and validated. Filtration partners contribute by understanding contamination risks, defining performance requirements, and engineering solutions that work within the physical and operational constraints of the aircraft.

That disciplined approach is valuable when emerging propulsion concepts move from laboratory development toward flight demonstration. Early attention to filtration can help teams identify contamination pathways, establish validation priorities, and integrate protective technologies before aircraft designs become difficult or costly to change.

An Innovation Legacy Built for What Comes Next

Across Pall’s history, the applications have changed, but the engineering objective has remained consistent: protect what matters so critical systems can perform as intended. The same mindset connects hydraulic filters on early jetliners, life support components used during Apollo 11, cabin air filtration, helicopter engine protection, sustainable aviation fuel testing, and filtration for hydrogen fuel cell propulsion.

For the aerospace sector, that continuity is instructive. New propulsion technologies will bring new design questions, but reliability will still depend on disciplined attention to every system interface. Contamination control will remain fundamental wherever air, fuel, lubricant, hydraulic fluid, or process gases must meet exacting requirements.

Pall’s aerospace legacy therefore is not simply a record of past milestones. It is a platform for the next generation of flight. As aviation pursues greater efficiency, new energy sources, and more sustainable operations, filtration will continue to work behind the scenes, protecting systems and enabling progress. The technology may remain largely unseen, but its contribution to aerospace performance, safety, and innovation is built into the journey.

title: Yusen Logistics and Finnair Strengthen Collaboration Through Sustainable Aviation Fuel Agreement
description:
Tokyo, and Helsinki, 14 September 2026 – Yusen Logistics and Finnair are pleased to announce an agreement concerning Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)-related environmental attributes.
Under the agreement, Yusen Logistics will purchase SAF-related environmental attributes from Finnair.
The initiative forms part of Yusen Logistics’ broader sustainability strategy and supports Finnair’s efforts to expand the use of SAF in aviation.
Eisuke Fukagawa, Head of Air Freight Forwarding Unit Yusen Logistics Global Management "Addressing emissions from global logistics requires collaboration across the transportation and supply chain ecosystem.
This initiative supports Yusen Logistics’ global sustainability strategy and provides customers with an additional way to support SAF use through allocated environmental attributes.
text:
Tokyo, and Helsinki, 14 September 2026 – Yusen Logistics and Finnair are pleased to announce an agreement concerning Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF)-related environmental attributes. Through this collaboration, the companies aim to support the reduction of lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions associated with air cargo transportation and contribute to efforts to decarbonize global supply chains.

Under the agreement, Yusen Logistics will purchase SAF-related environmental attributes from Finnair. The arrangement uses a Book-and-Claim mechanism, under which the environmental attributes associated with SAF use can be allocated separately from the physical movement of fuel and cargo.

The agreement was concluded with the support of Western Associates, Inc. (WAI), Finnair's General Sales Agent in Japan.

The initiative forms part of Yusen Logistics’ broader sustainability strategy and supports Finnair’s efforts to expand the use of SAF in aviation.

The companies recognize the importance of collaborative and scalable approaches that address emissions from air cargo transportation while maintaining reliable international logistics services.

Commitment on SAF-Related Environmental Attributes

The agreement reflects the shared ambition of Yusen Logistics and Finnair to support customers seeking ways to address emissions associated with air freight transportation through SAF-related environmental attributes and to support the aviation industry's transition toward lower-carbon operations.

The collaboration also demonstrates the importance of partnerships across the logistics ecosystem, bringing together airlines and logistics providers to support demand for SAF and contribute to the aviation industry’s broader decarbonization efforts.

Through this mechanism, customers can support the use of SAF. Participating customers may receive certificates and emissions-related reporting concerning the SAF environmental attributes allocated to them. These materials may support customers in understanding the relevant environmental attributes and in pursuing their sustainability objectives.

Executive Comments

"We are pleased to see our customers making a long-term commitment to the use of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). This multi-year agreement with Yusen Logistics is an important milestone in reducing the climate impact of air cargo and a concrete example of how customers and airlines can work together to accelerate the energy transition. By creating long-term demand for SAF, we can help support the growth of production and availability in the years ahead. We hope this commitment will also encourage other companies to explore how SAF can help reduce air cargo emissions."

Gabriela Hiitola

Senior Vice President

Finnair Cargo

"Our customers increasingly expect tangible and credible solutions to reduce the environmental impact of their supply chains. Through collaboration with Finnair, we can provide practical decarbonization options through a SAF Book-and-Claim mechanism while maintaining the high service quality our customers require. In addition, customers can benefit from transparency through certificates and reporting related to SAF environmental attributes, helping support their own sustainability objectives. This agreement is another important milestone in our sustainability journey."

Eisuke Fukagawa,

Head of Air Freight Forwarding Unit

Yusen Logistics Global Management

"Addressing emissions from global logistics requires collaboration across the transportation and supply chain ecosystem. This initiative supports Yusen Logistics’ global sustainability strategy and provides customers with an additional way to support SAF use through allocated environmental attributes. It also demonstrates the role that cooperation between airlines and logistics providers can play in supporting the aviation sector’s transition toward lower-carbon operations."

text:
LUND, Sweden, Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Alfa Laval has been selected by Saipem, the EPC (Engineering, Procurement, Construction) contractor for Stockholm Exergi's BECCS (Bioenergy with Carbon Capture and Storage) project to supply heat transfer equipment for one of Europe's largest bioenergy carbon capture facilities. The project is expected to begin operations in 2028 and will capture, liquify, and permanently store up to 800,000 tonnes of CO₂ annually, representing approximately one to two percent of today's total global carbon capture capacity.

Stockholm Exergi, a leading Swedish energy provider, is taking a bold step towards net-negative emissions with the first-of-its-kind large-scale BECCS initiative set to run at Europe's largest biomass-based combined heat and power plant in Stockholm. When fully operational, the facility will capture and store CO2 from the combustion of biogenic fuels, where Alfa Laval's heat transfer solutions will play a crucial role, maximizing system efficiency and heat recovery. The project is part of Sweden's climate neutrality goals, contributing to the EU's climate strategy and positioning Stockholm Exergi as an early adopter.

"Carbon capture at this scale is one of the most demanding thermal engineering challenges in the energy transition and effective energy recovery is what ultimately makes it commercially viable," says Thomas Møller, President of the Energy Division, Alfa Laval. "Stockholm Exergi is setting a new standard for what net-negative emissions can look like at industrial scale, and we are honoured to contribute to this landmark project with our heat transfer solutions."

"The plant will require a lot of energy to capture the CO2 from the flue gas and liquify it, but with the high quality Ziepack heat exchangers from Alfa Laval, we will be able to reclaim the energy used. This energy will go back in our existing district heating system, which contributes additionally to our carbon removal targets," says Egil Nybakk, Director BECCS at Stockholm Exergi.

Alfa Laval will supply its Ziepack gas-gas interchanger alongside multiple process plate-and-frame heat exchangers, crucial for maximizing system efficiency and heat recovery, and integral parts of the core capture process. The equipment package has been selected by Saipem as part of its EPC contract for the Stockholm Exergi BECCS facility. Alfa Laval's technologies will contribute to the efficiency of the carbon capture process and support the project's ambition to become one of the world's largest facilities for the capture and permanent storage of biogenic CO2.

text:
The UK Government has confirmed it will not impose anti‑subsidy duties on imports of hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO) biodiesel from the United States, despite a Trade Remedies Authority (TRA) finding that the fuel was subsidised and had caused injury to domestic producers.

In its final determination, published on 10 September, the TRA concluded that US‑origin HVO biodiesel benefited from subsidies and recommended fixed countervailing duties ranging from £258.10 to £266.68 per tonne (approximately €302–€312).

Under UK trade‑remedy rules, the TRA must also assess whether applying such duties would be in the UK’s economic interests.

In this case, it found that imposing a countervailing amount would not meet the economic interest test, citing disproportionate costs for downstream businesses, importers and consumers.

After reviewing the TRA’s findings and wider public‑interest considerations, the Secretary of State decided not to apply any anti‑subsidy measure. As a result, no duties will be levied on HVO biodiesel imported from the USA.

The investigation, launched in March 2025, covered biodiesel produced through synthesis or hydrotreatment of non‑fossil oils and fats, whether pure or blended.

Renewable diesel — also known as green diesel — falls within this scope, while synthetic paraffinic kerosene (sustainable aviation fuel) does not.

The UK currently has established FAME biodiesel production but no dedicated HVO manufacturing capacity.

The TRA’s economic interest test forms a mandatory part of most trade‑remedy investigations and assesses whether proposed measures support the broader UK economy.

text: When people talk about Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), the conversation often focuses on the refinery. But building a SAF ecosystem takes much more than that. Before SAF can power an aircraft, there is a much longer journey behind it. It starts with collecting the right feedstocks, including used cooking oil, and building the supply chain infrastructure needed to move them from collection points to processing facilities. It also requires the right technology, strong partnerships, long-term investment and internationally recognised sustainability certification. Most importantly, it takes time and commitment. No single company can build an entire SAF ecosystem alone. It takes collaboration across industries, governments, technology providers, investors and communities. At FatHopes Energy, our journey towards SAF started long before the refinery. It started with building collection networks and creating better pathways for waste to be recovered and given a second life. Building a SAF future doesn't happen overnight. The refinery is an important part of the journey, but it is only one part of a much bigger ecosystem. Because the journey to sustainable aviation doesn't start when an aircraft takes off. text:
On September 10, 2026, a container-based facility for the synthesis of green methanol was inaugurated at Stralsund University of Applied Sciences in the presence of Dr. Wolfgang Blank, Minister of Economic Affairs for the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. It is the result of the joint project “Decentralized Methanol Synthesis” involving the partners Leibniz Institute for Plasma Science and Technology e. V., TAB Maschinen- und Stahlbau GmbH Barth, Stralsund University of Applied Sciences, the Leibniz Institute for Catalysis e.V., and the Fraunhofer Institute for Ceramic Technologies and Systems.

The project is one of the subprojects of the WIR!2 alliance biogeniV for the utilization of biogenic residues. “Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania offers ideal conditions for generating electricity from renewable energy sources and processing it—along with biogenic waste materials—into innovative products for our economy,” said Dr. Wolfgang Blank. “The methanol synthesis plant is a prime example of this—and it’s ‘made in MV.’ “This project brings together science, industry, and regional resources—and it is precisely these kinds of collaborative projects that we need to ensure sustainable value creation and new jobs in the state, thereby capitalizing on the opportunities presented by the energy transition,” the minister continued.

The project partners designed the plant over the course of three years of collaborative work. It is designed for decentralized operation and is thus suited for the typical applications of on-farm biogas plants. In the plant, CO₂ and hydrogen are converted—via catalysis at approximately 240 degrees Celsius and an elevated pressure of 40 bar—into a methanol-water mixture, from which the water is subsequently separated. The pressure conditions within the system are specifically controlled to ensure that the thermal processes proceed stably. “The process demonstrates that we can store green—that is, renewable—hydrogen in a liquid form—with the option of potentially transporting it worldwide,” explains Prof. Dr. Johannes Gulden from the Institute for Renewable Energy Systems at Stralsund University of Applied Sciences.

The further expansion of the facility is the focus of a sister project that has just been launched. In addition to scaling up the process, the project aims to further develop the entire process chain: Plans include the processing of biogas and the separation of the CO₂ it contains using membrane technology, a plasma stage for optimizing the methanol synthesis process, an electrolysis plant for local hydrogen production, and the subsequent concentration of the methanol. The goal is to deploy the technology directly at a biogas plant and make the produced methanol available for agricultural use. This demonstration plant is expected to achieve a production capacity of up to 36 liters of methanol per day.

Launched in 2022 as “Biogenic Waste Utilization for the Green Transformation,” the biogeniV consortium project is funded as part of the WIR! “Change Through Innovation in the Region” program of the Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space, as well as regionally in eastern Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania. Across all subprojects, it involves more than 55 partners from industry, research, and local governments.

“We see green methanol from the region as a key building block for a resilient and climate-friendly future,” says Michael Galander. The mayor of the Hanseatic City of Anklam is the alliance’s spokesperson: “We have large quantities of these residual materials available in our region and can also provide the necessary green electricity from wind and solar power.”

Pengembangan SAF tersebut menjadi salah satu bagian dari aktivitas Pertamina Patra Niaga di Kilang Cilacap, Jawa Tengah. Fasilitas ini menjadi bagian penting dalam ekosistem energi Pertamina sekaligus salah satu lokasi pengembangan bahan bakar penerbangan berbasis bahan baku berkelanjutan.

Pengembangan SAF diperkenalkan kepada jurnalis dari berbagai wilayah operasional Pertamina Patra Niaga dalam agenda Pertamina Media Xpose (Pertamax) Journey 2026 di Cilacap, Kamis (10/9/2026). Kegiatan tersebut memberikan kesempatan kepada awak media untuk melihat lebih dekat pengembangan energi rendah emisi dan peran Kilang Cilacap dalam mendukung transformasi energi.

Vice President Corporate Communication Pertamina Patra Niaga, Kitty Andhora, mengatakan Kilang Cilacap merupakan salah satu fasilitas strategis dalam ekosistem energi Pertamina. Dengan kapasitas pengolahan mencapai 348 ribu barel per hari, kilang tersebut memiliki peran penting dalam mendukung ketahanan energi nasional.

“Kilang Cilacap menjadi salah satu fasilitas strategis dalam ekosistem energi Pertamina. Dengan kapasitas pengolahan mencapai 348 ribu barel per hari, kilang ini memiliki peran penting dalam mendukung ketahanan energi nasional,” ujar Kitty.

Selain menjalankan fungsi pengolahan energi, Kilang Cilacap diproyeksikan menjadi proyek green refinery pertama di Indonesia yang berfokus pada produksi bahan bakar ramah lingkungan dalam skala besar. Pengembangan tersebut diharapkan dapat memperkuat kemandirian energi hijau sekaligus mendukung pengembangan SAF nasional.

Salah satu aspek yang menjadi perhatian dalam pengembangan SAF adalah pemanfaatan UCO sebagai bahan baku. Minyak jelantah yang sebelumnya dipandang sebagai limbah dapat dimanfaatkan kembali dan masuk ke dalam rantai nilai energi.

Pemanfaatan tersebut membuka peluang penerapan prinsip ekonomi sirkular, sekaligus menghadirkan alternatif bahan bakar penerbangan yang lebih berkelanjutan. Dengan demikian, pengembangan SAF tidak hanya berkaitan dengan penyediaan bahan bakar bagi sektor penerbangan, tetapi juga dengan pemanfaatan sumber daya secara lebih efisien.

Menurut Kitty, pengembangan SAF merupakan bagian dari upaya Pertamina Patra Niaga menghadirkan produk dan layanan energi yang relevan dengan perkembangan industri. Hal tersebut termasuk menjawab kebutuhan sektor penerbangan terhadap bahan bakar yang lebih berkelanjutan.

“Bagi kami, keberlanjutan dan ketahanan energi bukan dua hal yang berjalan sendiri-sendiri. Keduanya perlu dibangun secara bersamaan,” kata Kitty.

text:
(4 Minutes Read)

Swiss cleantech company plans large-scale Sun-to-Liquid facility in southern Morocco, targeting 100,000 tonnes of renewable fuel production annually

The global aviation, shipping and road-transport sectors are under increasing pressure to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels and accelerate the transition toward lower-carbon alternatives. While electrification is advancing rapidly in road transport, sectors such as aviation and long-distance shipping remain difficult to decarbonize because of their high energy requirements and the limitations of current battery technology.

Renewable synthetic fuels, also known as e-fuels or Power-to-Liquid fuels, are emerging as one potential solution. These fuels can be produced using renewable energy and carbon-containing feedstocks and can, in principle, be used in existing engines and fuel infrastructure with limited modifications.

Against this backdrop, Zurich-based cleantech company Synhelion has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Government of Morocco to explore the development of a large-scale commercial plant for the production of renewable synthetic fuels.

Under the agreement, Synhelion plans to develop a facility in Morocco’s southern Tan-Tan province with an estimated investment of USD 1 billion. The proposed plant is expected to have an annual production capacity of approximately 100,000 tonnes of renewable fuel.

Synhelion has already taken steps to establish a presence in the country. The company has reserved land for the proposed facility and established a local branch in Morocco, laying the groundwork for the project’s potential development.

The proposed location is considered attractive because of Morocco’s substantial renewable-energy resources, particularly its strong solar-energy potential. These resources could provide the energy required for Synhelion’s technology while supporting the development of a broader renewable-fuel value chain within the country.

“Morocco’s exceptional renewable energy resources and its clear industrial strategy make it an ideal location for scaling our synthetic fuel technology,” said Gianluca Ambrosetti, Co-CEO and Co-Founder of Synhelion.

Moroccan officials have also highlighted the project’s potential to support investment, technological innovation and industrial development. “This MoU reflects Morocco’s ambition to attract high-impact investments that combine innovation, sustainability and industrial development,” said Karim Zidane, Morocco’s Minister of Investment.

Synhelion is developing Sun-to-Liquid technology designed to produce renewable synthetic fuels for sectors including aviation, road transportation and marine transport. The company’s process uses high-temperature heat generated from renewable electricity to transform a combination of biomethane, carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water into syngas. This syngas is then further processed and refined into liquid fuels, including renewable jet fuel, diesel and gasoline. A key element of the technology is its integrated thermal-energy storage system. By storing thermal energy, the facility can continue producing fuel even when renewable electricity generation fluctuates. This is particularly important for large-scale industrial fuel production, where continuous operation can improve efficiency and reliability.

The proposed Synhelion project also fits into Morocco’s broader strategy of attracting investment in renewable energy, green industries and low-carbon technologies. The country has invested heavily in expanding its renewable-energy capacity and has positioned itself as a potential hub for the production and export of clean fuels.

For Synhelion, establishing a large commercial facility in Morocco could provide an important opportunity to demonstrate its technology at industrial scale. The planned 100,000-tonne annual capacity would represent a significant step beyond pilot and demonstration projects and could help establish a commercial supply chain for renewable synthetic fuels.

title: Frontex-backed returns top 33,000 in first half of 2026 - ETIAS.com
description:
14 Sep 2026 Frontex supported more than 33,000 returns from European Union Member States to non-EU countries in the first half of 2026, up from around 30,000 during the same period in 2025.
That was up from about 19,000 voluntary returns a year earlier.
Since 2022, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency has supported around 215,000 returns.
The agency recorded 24,000 supported returns in 2022, followed by 39,000 in 2023 and 56,000 in 2024.
The total reached 63,000 in 2025, then surpassed 33,000 in the first six months of 2026.
text:
14 Sep 2026

Frontex supported more than 33,000 returns from European Union Member States to non-EU countries in the first half of 2026, up from around 30,000 during the same period in 2025.

Around two-thirds were voluntary, with roughly 21,000 people choosing to comply with return decisions between January and June. That was up from about 19,000 voluntary returns a year earlier.

The rise comes as the EU changes its legal framework for returns and prepares to consider a stronger role for Frontex. Since 2022, the European Border and Coast Guard Agency has supported around 215,000 returns.

Returns climb for fourth straight year

Frontex’s figures show a steady rise in the number of people returned with its support.

The agency recorded 24,000 supported returns in 2022, followed by 39,000 in 2023 and 56,000 in 2024. The total reached 63,000 in 2025, then surpassed 33,000 in the first six months of 2026.

Every Frontex-supported return follows an enforceable return decision, meaning the person has exhausted their legal options to remain in the EU.

National authorities decide whether a return will be voluntary or forced. Frontex supports both types but does not make that decision itself.

In a voluntary return, a person complies with the obligation to leave and may receive practical assistance and, when eligible, financial support. A forced return takes place when the person has not complied with that obligation.

Frontex considers voluntary returns generally more cost-effective because forced operations routinely require escorts, medical and monitoring staff and, in some cases, dedicated charter arrangements.

Hans Leijtens, Frontex Executive Director, has tied effective returns to the credibility of the wider migration system. He has also stressed that returns should take place lawfully, safely, and with dignity, with greater attention to helping people prepare before departure.

More staff support return operations

The growing number of returns has been accompanied by a larger Frontex presence in Member States.

During the first half of 2026, 109 Return Specialists worked across 15 Member States. Their work includes explaining available return options, helping national authorities manage cases in return-processing systems, and assisting with efforts to obtain identity documents from authorities in countries of origin.

That deployment rose from 95 Return Specialists during the same period in 2025.

Frontex also deployed 118 Return Escort and Support Officers (FRESOs) across 11 Member States in the first half of the year, up from 102 the year earlier.

FRESOs accompany returnees, help them navigate airports, and handle administrative and logistical tasks related to flights. Their work can also cover voluntary returnees who need additional assistance.

(Image courtesy of Rocker Sta via Unsplash)

Reintegration support expands

Frontex-backed operations can continue after a person arrives in their country of origin.

Around 14,000 people registered for EU reintegration assistance during the first six months of 2026, up from around 8,000 during the same period a year earlier. More than four in five registrants had returned voluntarily.

Assistance can include vocational training, counseling, or a small grant to help start a business.

The reintegration total does not directly match the number of people returned with Frontex support. Member States can also enroll other eligible returnees in the EU Reintegration Program.

New EU rules reshape return policy

The increase in Frontex-supported returns comes as EU institutions put a new common framework in place.

The European Parliament and Council agreed in June 2026 on the Regulation establishing a Common European System for Returns. The rules create common standards across the EU and make forced return the rule in certain cases, including when a person does not cooperate, absconds to another Member State, or poses a security risk.

Magnus Brunner, European Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, has argued that return numbers need to rise substantially. He has described the new rules as a stronger framework for expanding those efforts.

Another policy change could follow soon. The European Commission is expected to propose a further strengthening of Frontex’s mandate on returns, including its support for Member States, in autumn 2026.

(Image courtesy of Guillaume Périgois via Unsplash)

Germany leads Frontex-backed returns

Germany, France, Cyprus, Belgium and Sweden recorded the highest numbers of Frontex-supported returns between January and June 2026.

Frontex did not provide individual totals for each of those countries.

The 10 most common nationalities among people returned with Frontex support were Türkiye, Syria, Georgia, Colombia, India, Brazil, Albania, Morocco, Nigeria, and Iraq. The agency likewise did not provide separate totals by nationality in the figures it released.

Return flights add environmental focus

Air travel accounts for most Frontex return operations, and the agency has also been working to reduce the environmental footprint of those flights.

Frontex prioritizes scheduled services over charter flights when operational conditions allow. Under an agreement in place since 2023 with a major European airline, part of the airline’s revenue from Frontex-funded flights goes toward Sustainable Aviation Fuel and other environmental initiatives that meet International Civil Aviation Organization sustainability criteria.

During the first half of 2026, that arrangement funded more than 90 tonnes of Sustainable Aviation Fuel. Frontex estimated that the purchase mitigated 313 tonnes of carbon dioxide across the fuel’s full lifecycle.

(Image courtesy of Aron Marinelli via Unsplash)

Return data meets digital border management

Frontex’s return operations rely on case-processing systems and reliable identity documents, making accurate migration data increasingly important as EU border management becomes more digital.

That may create operational connections with systems such as the Entry/Exit System (EES) and the upcoming European Travel Information and Authorization System (ETIAS).

However, available information does not indicate that Frontex returns data feeds directly to either system, nor that higher return numbers would improve their performance.

Bigger system faces next policy test

The first-half figures point to a return system that now stretches well beyond the act of departure. Voluntary returns remain the largest category, while Frontex has expanded staffing, logistical support and reintegration assistance as EU institutions tighten the rules governing noncompliance.

For Member States and Frontex, any further rise in returns would put pressure on several parts of that structure at once, from case management and identity-document work to escorts, flights and post-return support.

The next major test will come with the European Commission’s planned proposal in autumn 2026 to strengthen Frontex’s returns mandate. Future data will also show whether voluntary departures continue to make up most Frontex-supported returns as the new EU framework develops.

text:
Airbus is moving forward with its “Wing of Tomorrow’ research that aligns closely with the development of its next commercial aircraft.

As part of these studies, the manufacturer aims to bring lab research to the sky with the launch of flight test campaigns involving an A321neo.

The A321neo, which is fitted with long and high-span wing extensions, is designed to explore how much efficiency a next-generation single-aisle could squeeze from the wings alone.

Revealed at the Farnborough Airshow, this is part of a three-year programme on the path to finding the successor to the A320neo and ensuring a new single-aisle reaches market by the late-2030s.

What Airbus Is Testing: Long and High-Span Wings

Over the next three years, Airbus will design, build, and flight-test full-scale wing extensions that can be attached to the A321neo’s existing wings. This turns the aircraft into a flying demonstrator with wings that are not only longer but also slender.

The extensions, to be several metres long, will replicate a folding wing tip but in its fully extended position during flight. This test campaign will not involve actual in-flight folding, but implementing this structure is important to yield data.

These extensions, Airbus has said, are to be densely instrumented and will see sensors capturing loads, vibrations, and other aerodynamic behaviour across the flight envelope, including handling. The goal for the manufacturer and its team is to see how the higher-aspect-ratio wings, and thus the longer span, behave in real-world operating conditions.

Furthermore, Airbus is interested in understanding how the wings affect the climb performance of planes, whether they impact cruise efficiency, and what the stability of the A321neo looks like in comparison to the current wing configuration.

Sue Partridge, the head of the Wing of Tomorrow programme at Airbus, said the campaign will allow the planemaker to safely challenge the traditional design limits that have been in place and additionally explore the benefits of longer wings.

Partridge says that one of the biggest levers that is available to improve flight efficiency is the wing. Currently, digital modelling and wind tunnel testing are only taking the studies so far; the modelling will then finalise the extension geometries and determine which flight tests will take place.

How This Feeds Into The New Airbus Aircraft

Airbus has been open about the technology that it’s looking to stack and study, centring on the next-generation single-aisle in the works. This openness flags both the availability and the challenges that come with it.

At the 2025 Airbus Summit, the company outlined a concept that would aim to deliver a 20-30% fuel-efficiency gain over the current A320neo jets, with entry into service hoped for the late-2030s. This platform would also be capable of flying on up to 100% sustainable aviation fuel.

The concepts look to include long, foldable composite wings with higher aspect ratios than what’s found in today’s A320 wings to cut induced drag and boost cruise efficiency. Additionally, there have been studies into what more efficient engines are on the market, such as disruptive open-fan designs like the CFM RISE, which are being flight tested on an A380 propulsion demonstrator later this decade.

Airbus is also conducting its due diligence into hybrid-electric and hydrogen-ready power systems, what types of next-gen batteries are available, and how ultra-light structural materials could be adopted to bring costs down and extract efficiency improvements wherever possible.

Ultimately, while there is still much work to get the next single-aisle ready for launch, the Wing of Tomorrow plays an integral role in the roadmap, allowing technologies to mature and studies to return data that can then be analysed and possibly explored further for full-scale adoption.

Di Kilang Cilacap, perjalanan itu telah dimulai.
text:
TERASMALUKU.COM,-CILACAP-Minyak goreng bekas biasanya memiliki nasib sederhana. Setelah berkali-kali digunakan, warnanya menghitam, aromanya berubah, lalu dibuang. Tetapi bagaimana jika minyak yang dianggap sudah tidak berguna itu justru menjadi bagian dari perjalanan sebuah pesawat? Pertanyaan itu menemukan jawabannya di Cilacap, Jawa Tengah.

Di kompleks kilang yang selama puluhan tahun menjadi salah satu penopang kebutuhan energi Indonesia, minyak jelantah atau Used Cooking Oil (UCO) kini mendapat peran baru. Bahan yang berasal dari aktivitas sehari-hari masyarakat itu dikembangkan sebagai salah satu bahan baku Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan.

Dari dapur, minyak jelantah memasuki rantai pengumpulan. Dari sana, ia menjalani proses pengolahan dan pengujian sebelum menjadi bagian dari bahan bakar yang dapat digunakan untuk penerbangan. Perjalanan tersebut memperlihatkan satu perubahan penting dalam cara energi dipandang: sesuatu yang sebelumnya dianggap limbah dapat kembali memiliki nilai ketika ditempatkan dalam teknologi dan rantai industri yang tepat.

Cerita itu menjadi salah satu yang dibawa Pertamina Patra Niaga ketika sekitar 60 awak media nasional dari berbagai wilayah Indonesia berkunjung ke PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Refinery Unit (RU) Cilacap dalam rangkaian Pertamina Media Xpose (Pertamax) Journey 2026, Kamis (10/9/2026).

Kunjungan tersebut bukan hanya tentang melihat bagaimana sebuah kilang bekerja. Lebih jauh, para jurnalis diajak melihat bagaimana industri energi berusaha menjaga kebutuhan energi saat ini sekaligus mempersiapkan sumber energi yang lebih berkelanjutan untuk masa depan.

Pengembangan SAF tidak muncul tanpa alasan. Industri penerbangan menghadapi tantangan besar dalam upaya mengurangi emisi karbon. Pesawat membutuhkan bahan bakar dengan karakteristik tertentu dan belum dapat begitu saja mengganti seluruh kebutuhan energinya dengan sumber energi lain. Karena itu, SAF menjadi salah satu pilihan yang dikembangkan di berbagai negara.

Organisasi Penerbangan Sipil Internasional atau ICAO menempatkan SAF sebagai salah satu elemen penting dalam upaya menekan emisi sektor penerbangan. Bahan bakar ini dapat dibuat dari berbagai sumber terbarukan maupun limbah, sepanjang memenuhi persyaratan teknis dan keberlanjutan yang ditetapkan.

Indonesia mulai mengambil bagian dalam perkembangan tersebut. Pada Agustus 2025, Pertamina mencatat penerbangan komersial Pelita Air rute Jakarta-Denpasar menggunakan SAF berbasis UCO. Pemerintah menyebut penggunaan tersebut sebagai bagian dari pengembangan bahan bakar penerbangan berkelanjutan di Indonesia.

SAF yang dikembangkan Pertamina diproduksi di RU IV Cilacap. Fakta itu membuat minyak jelantah memperoleh cerita baru. Bukan lagi sekadar sisa minyak dari penggorengan, tetapi bahan yang dapat masuk ke dalam rantai nilai energi. Tentu perubahannya tidak berlangsung seketika.

Ada proses pengumpulan bahan baku, pengolahan, pengujian kualitas, pemenuhan standar hingga pengawasan rantai pasok. Semua tahapan tersebut menjadi bagian dari perjalanan sebelum bahan baku tersebut dapat digunakan untuk menghasilkan bahan bakar penerbangan.

Executive General Manager RU Cilacap, Hermawan Budiantoro, menyebut pengembangan PertaminaSAF sebagai salah satu bentuk inovasi para pekerja kilang.“PertaminaSAF menjadi bukti bahwa Perwira Pertamina tak henti berinovasi, memanfaatkan kembali minyak jelantah menjadi bahan bakar yang lebih ramah lingkungan,” ujarnya.

Menurut Hermawan, inovasi tersebut memperlihatkan bahwa kilang tidak hanya berperan memenuhi kebutuhan energi saat ini, tetapi juga menyiapkan solusi energi yang lebih berkelanjutan. Untuk memahami arti inovasi tersebut, para jurnalis tidak hanya mendapat penjelasan di dalam ruangan. Mereka diajak melihat langsung fasilitas Kilang Cilacap.

Rangkaian kunjungan diawali dengan paparan mengenai operasional dan peran kilang di Patra Graha. Para jurnalis mendapatkan gambaran tentang proses bisnis, produk yang dihasilkan, aspek keselamatan, keandalan operasi serta kontribusi kilang terhadap kebutuhan energi nasional. Setelah itu, rombongan bergerak memasuki kawasan kilang.

Para jurnalis juga dibawa ke Control Room RU IV Cilacap sebagai bagian dari infrastruktur operasi kilang. Pintu ruang kontrol menjadi salah satu titik yang memperlihatkan sisi berbeda dari Kilang Cilacap. Di ruangan itu, kesibukan kilang tidak selalu terlihat dalam bentuk pekerja yang bergerak dari satu fasilitas ke fasilitas lain. Sebagian besar proses justru berlangsung di balik layar, dipantau melalui deretan layar dan sistem kendali yang menampilkan kondisi operasi.

Di hadapan operator, angka dan grafik bukan sekadar tampilan di layar. Setiap perubahan menunjukkan kondisi tertentu dari proses yang sedang berlangsung. Temperatur, tekanan, aliran dan berbagai parameter operasi harus dipantau agar proses berjalan sesuai batas yang ditetapkan.

Dari ruangan tersebut, operator memantau jalannya proses pengolahan yang berlangsung di area kilang. Suasana ruang kontrol relatif tenang. Namun ketenangan itu bukan berarti tidak ada pekerjaan. Justru di ruangan inilah ketelitian menjadi bagian penting dari pekerjaan. Operator harus membaca kondisi operasi, memastikan parameter tetap terkendali dan merespons apabila muncul indikasi yang membutuhkan perhatian.

Bagi para jurnalis yang mengikuti Pertamax Journey 2026, ruang kontrol memberikan gambaran bahwa proses menghasilkan energi tidak hanya berlangsung di balik pipa-pipa besar yang terlihat dari luar. Ada sistem kendali dan manusia yang bekerja bersamaan untuk memastikan operasi tetap berjalan.

Pemandangan itu sekaligus mengubah cara melihat sebuah kilang. Dari luar, kompleks Kilang Cilacap tampak sebagai hamparan fasilitas industri dengan tangki, pipa dan berbagai instalasi. Namun di baliknya terdapat ruang yang menjadi salah satu pusat pemantauan operasi.

Di sinilah teknologi bertemu dengan pengalaman manusia. Layar memberikan data secara terus-menerus. Namun keputusan tetap membutuhkan operator yang memahami kondisi proses dan prosedur operasi. Keandalan energi, pada akhirnya, tidak hanya ditentukan oleh besarnya kapasitas sebuah kilang.

Ia juga bergantung pada ketelitian orang-orang yang menjaga agar proses tersebut tetap berjalan aman dan andal. Dari ruang kontrol itulah sebagian perjalanan energi dapat dilihat—dari bahan baku yang masuk, proses pengolahan yang berlangsung, hingga produk yang nantinya digunakan masyarakat.

Di tengah kompleksitas instalasi pengolahan dan berbagai infrastruktur pendukung, satu hal terasa jelas: menyediakan energi dalam jumlah besar membutuhkan proses yang panjang. Energi yang sampai ke masyarakat dalam bentuk BBM ternyata tidak hadir begitu saja. Di belakangnya terdapat fasilitas pengolahan, sistem pengawasan, pekerja dengan keahlian khusus, prosedur keselamatan dan rangkaian operasi yang harus berjalan secara andal.

Kilang Cilacap memiliki kapasitas pengolahan mencapai 348 ribu barel per hari. Dalam pemaparan Pertamina, fasilitas tersebut menopang sekitar 34 persen kebutuhan BBM nasional dan 60 persen kebutuhan BBM di Pulau Jawa.

Angka tersebut memberikan gambaran mengenai posisi strategis Cilacap dalam sistem energi nasional. “​​Kami ingin memastikan rekan-rekan media mendapatkan gambaran utuh bahwa energi yang digunakan masyarakat setiap hari melalui proses yang panjang dan membutuhkan keandalan operasi, disiplin, serta penerapan aspek keselamatan yang tinggi,” kata Hermawan.

Di balik angka-angka tersebut ada pekerjaan yang tidak selalu terlihat oleh masyarakat. Para Perwira kilang harus memastikan fasilitas berjalan, keselamatan terjaga dan proses pengolahan berlangsung sesuai standar. Pada saat yang sama, mereka juga dituntut untuk terus mencari cara baru agar fasilitas energi dapat menjawab perubahan kebutuhan.

Di sinilah cerita Kilang Cilacap menjadi lebih besar daripada sekadar cerita tentang sebuah fasilitas pengolahan BBM. Ada dua kebutuhan yang berjalan bersamaan. Yang pertama adalah ketahanan energi.

Indonesia masih membutuhkan BBM dalam jumlah besar untuk menggerakkan transportasi, industri dan berbagai aktivitas masyarakat. Karena itu, keandalan kilang tetap menjadi bagian penting dalam menjaga pasokan energi.

Yang kedua adalah tuntutan keberlanjutan. Dunia bergerak menuju sistem energi yang lebih rendah emisi. Industri pun dituntut mencari teknologi, bahan baku dan proses yang dapat mengurangi dampak lingkungan. Kedua kebutuhan tersebut tidak selalu mudah dipertemukan. Namun, Pertamina mencoba menempatkan keduanya dalam satu perjalanan.

VP Corporate Communication Pertamina Patra Niaga, Kitty Andhora, mengatakan Kilang Cilacap merupakan salah satu fasilitas strategis dalam ekosistem energi Pertamina.“Dengan kapasitas pengolahan mencapai 348 ribu barel per hari, kilang ini memiliki peran penting dalam mendukung ketahanan energi nasional,” jelas Kitty.

Ia mengatakan pengembangan SAF menjadi salah satu topik yang diperkenalkan kepada media dalam Pertamax Journey 2026. “Bagi kami, keberlanjutan dan ketahanan energi bukan dua hal yang berjalan sendiri-sendiri. Keduanya perlu dibangun secara bersamaan,” katanya.

Kilang Cilacap sendiri diproyeksikan menjadi proyek green refinery yang diarahkan untuk memproduksi bahan bakar ramah lingkungan dalam skala besar. Pengembangan SAF berbasis UCO menjadi salah satu bagian dari perjalanan tersebut.

Ada sisi lain dari SAF yang menarik perhatian. Bahan bakunya dapat berasal dari sesuatu yang sangat dekat dengan kehidupan masyarakat: minyak goreng bekas. Selama ini, minyak jelantah kerap dianggap tidak lagi mempunyai nilai. Padahal, jika dibuang sembarangan, limbah tersebut juga berpotensi menimbulkan persoalan lingkungan. Pengumpulan UCO membuka kemungkinan lain.

Minyak bekas tersebut dapat dikumpulkan dan masuk ke dalam rantai pasok bahan baku energi. Dengan demikian, nilai ekonominya tidak berhenti setelah digunakan untuk menggoreng makanan. Konsep tersebut sejalan dengan prinsip ekonomi sirkular, yakni mengupayakan agar sumber daya dapat digunakan kembali dan memiliki nilai lebih panjang dalam sebuah rantai produksi.

Kementerian ESDM mencatat pengembangan SAF berbasis UCO di Indonesia juga melibatkan ekosistem pengumpulan minyak jelantah. Artinya, cerita SAF tidak hanya berada di dalam kompleks kilang. Ada masyarakat yang menghasilkan minyak jelantah. Ada pihak yang mengumpulkannya. Ada proses pengolahan. Ada pekerja yang menjalankan fasilitas. Ada pengujian dan standar yang harus dipenuhi.

Sebuah produk energi yang terlihat sederhana di ujungnya ternyata memiliki rantai perjalanan yang panjang. Dan justru di situlah letak perubahan besarnya. Limbah yang sebelumnya berhenti sebagai sisa konsumsi dapat kembali masuk ke dalam sebuah siklus produksi.

Corporate Secretary Pertamina Patra Niaga, Roberth Dumatubun, melihat inovasi dan keandalan operasi sebagai bagian yang tidak terpisahkan dari peran Kilang Cilacap. “Kilang Cilacap memiliki peran yang sangat penting dalam ekosistem energi Pertamina. Apa yang dilakukan para Perwira di sini, mulai dari menjaga keandalan operasi, memastikan aspek keselamatan, hingga menghadirkan berbagai inovasi, memberikan kontribusi nyata bagi ketahanan energi nasional,” tuturnya.

Sementara Direktur Armada dan Logistik Pertamina Patra Niaga, Arif Yunianto, menekankan pentingnya peran media dalam membawa cerita tersebut kepada masyarakat. “Media memiliki peran yang sangat penting dalam menyampaikan informasi kepada masyarakat. Berbagai pencapaian Pertamina, termasuk inovasi yang lahir dari para Perwira di lapangan, perlu diketahui publik,” ujarnya.

Pernyataan itu menjadi relevan dengan tujuan Pertamax Journey 2026. Sebab, ada jarak yang cukup jauh antara energi dan orang yang menggunakannya. Masyarakat mengisi kendaraan di SPBU tanpa harus melihat bagaimana BBM diproduksi. Penumpang pesawat naik ke kabin tanpa perlu mengetahui perjalanan panjang bahan bakar yang menggerakkan mesin pesawat.

Kunjungan ke Cilacap membuka sebagian kecil dari ruang yang selama ini berada di balik layar itu. Di sana, energi tidak hanya berbicara mengenai minyak dan mesin. Energi juga berbicara mengenai manusia, teknologi, keselamatan dan keputusan tentang bagaimana sumber daya akan digunakan.

SAF bukan solusi tunggal bagi seluruh persoalan emisi sektor penerbangan. Pengembangannya masih membutuhkan ketersediaan bahan baku, teknologi, infrastruktur, standar keberlanjutan dan ekosistem industri yang mampu menopang produksinya dalam jangka panjang.

Karena itu, keberhasilan mengembangkan SAF berbasis UCO bukanlah garis akhir. Ia adalah salah satu titik dalam perjalanan panjang. Begitu pula dengan Kilang Cilacap. Di satu sisi, fasilitas ini masih memikul tanggung jawab besar memenuhi kebutuhan energi masyarakat. Di sisi lain, ia mulai memasuki babak baru ketika teknologi dan inovasi diarahkan untuk menghasilkan bahan bakar yang lebih berkelanjutan.

Dua perjalanan itu kini bertemu. Ketahanan energi dan keberlanjutan tidak lagi ditempatkan sebagai dua cerita yang terpisah. Minyak jelantah menjadi salah satu contoh paling sederhana. Dari dapur, ia dikumpulkan. Dari tempat pengumpulan, ia masuk ke rantai energi. Setelah melalui proses yang panjang, ia dapat menjadi bagian dari bahan bakar penerbangan.

Pada akhirnya, cerita tentang SAF bukan hanya tentang bagaimana minyak jelantah bisa terbang. Cerita ini tentang bagaimana sebuah limbah diberi kesempatan kedua. Tentang bagaimana teknologi mengubah sesuatu yang sederhana menjadi bagian dari solusi.

Dan tentang bagaimana industri energi perlahan menatap masa depan tanpa meninggalkan tugasnya menjaga energi hari ini. Di Kilang Cilacap, perjalanan itu telah dimulai. Dari minyak jelantah menuju langit. Dan perjalanan tersebut masih jauh dari selesai.

text:
Scott Kirby has a plan to fight climate change in the sky — and he wants your tax dollars to fund it.

United's CEO says sustainable aviation fuel needs government subsidies to survive, just like solar and wind did years ago. Pump in the incentives now, he argues, and costs will eventually come down on their own.

Here's the catch. That "green" fuel currently makes up less than 1% of aviation fuel used worldwide. Some analysts say certain subsidy programs cost close to $1,000 for every ton of carbon dioxide they claim to prevent.

And United isn't a neutral bystander here. The airline owns a third of a fund that invests directly in this fuel technology — so subsidies wouldn't just help the planet, they'd help United's bottom line too.

Kirby says it's the only way sustainable fuel will ever work. Critics say there are cheaper, faster ways to cut airline emissions — better flight routing, avoiding contrails, direct carbon capture — that don't require a taxpayer check.

text:
REPUBLIKA.CO.ID, CILACAP, – PT Pertamina Patra Niaga memproyeksikan Kilang Cilacap menjadi proyek green refinery pertama di Indonesia yang difokuskan untuk memproduksi bahan bakar ramah lingkungan dalam skala besar. Proyek strategis ini diharapkan menjadi tonggak penting dalam memperkuat kemandirian energi hijau nasional, termasuk Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF).

“Bagi kami, keberlanjutan dan ketahanan energi bukan dua hal yang berjalan sendiri-sendiri. Keduanya perlu dibangun secara bersamaan,” ujar VP Corporate Communication Pertamina Patra Niaga, Kitty Andhora, di Cilacap, Jawa Tengah, Kamis.

Dengan demikian, Kilang Cilacap berperan strategis dalam memperkuat kemandirian Energi Hijau dan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Nasional. Pemanfaatan bahan baku Used Cooking Oil (UCO) atau minyak jelantah dalam pengembangan SAF juga membuka peluang pemanfaatan sumber daya yang sebelumnya merupakan limbah menjadi bagian dari rantai nilai energi.

Langkah tersebut sejalan dengan upaya mendorong penerapan prinsip ekonomi sirkular sekaligus menghadirkan alternatif bahan bakar penerbangan yang lebih berkelanjutan. Menurut Kitty, pengembangan SAF merupakan bagian dari perjalanan Pertamina Patra Niaga dalam menghadirkan produk dan layanan energi yang relevan dengan perkembangan industri, termasuk kebutuhan sektor penerbangan terhadap bahan bakar yang lebih berkelanjutan.

Target Operasi 2029 dan Dampak Ekonomi

Pertamina melalui Kilang Unit IV Cilacap menyebutkan proyek kilang bioavtur untuk bahan bakar minyak pesawat udara ramah lingkungan (SAF) berpotensi mendongkrak produk domestik bruto (PDB) sebesar Rp199 triliun per tahun. “Kami target proyek itu jalan pada 2027,” kata Executive General Manager Pertamina Patra Niaga Kilang Cilacap, Hermawan Budiantoro, di sela meninjau realisasi program Desa Energi Berdikari di Dusun Bondan, Kecamatan Kampung Laut, Cilacap, Kamis.

Pembangunan kilang bioavtur yang berada pada lahan seluas 17,5 hektare di dekat Kilang Unit IV Cilacap itu diperkirakan membutuhkan total nilai investasi mencapai 1,1 miliar dolar AS dengan target operasi pada 2029. Saat ini, kapasitas produksi bioavtur (SAF) mencapai 27 kiloliter per hari pada unit Unit Thermal Distillate Hydro Treating (TDHT) Cilacap sebagai penghasil avtur.

Dengan adanya kilang bioavtur itu nantinya kapasitas produksi meningkat 860 kiloliter per hari sehingga menjadi 887 kiloliter per hari pada 2029. Tak hanya menambah kontribusi kepada PDB, produksi BBM ramah lingkungan itu juga berpotensi mengurangi emisi tahunan sebesar 600 ribu ton setara karbon dioksida (CO2e) serta menyerap tenaga kerja estimasi sebanyak 5.900 orang.

title: United Kingdom Joins Canada and More Countries Participating at SAF Global Summit ...
description:
